beliefs: f advances the final character of the string to the next Unicode code point, leaving the rest unchanged [E1, E2, E3, E4, E5]
The advance is by Unicode code point order, not ASCII: é->ê, ç->è, ñ->ò, ü->ý, ÿ->Ā, ß->à, þ->ÿ, œ->Ŕ [E5]
Non-ASCII letters are advanced too (Greek, Cyrillic, accented Latin), so the letter test is Unicode-aware [E4, E5]
Strings ending in non-letters (digits, symbols, spaces, emoji, non-breaking space) are returned unchanged [E1, E2, E3, E4]
Case is preserved for ASCII: uppercase advances within uppercase, lowercase within lowercase, with z->a and Z->A [E1, E2, E3]
ASCII wrap-around is special (z->a, Z->A) rather than code-point increment, while non-ASCII letters just increment by one code point [E1, E3, E5]
